title: Tanzanian Smoked Fish
community: Lake Victoria regions and inland Tanzania
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Samaki wa Kuvuta Moshi — fish slow-smoked over wood or charcoal until deeply golden, dried, and intensely flavoured. The preserved fish tradition of Lake Victoria — smoked tilapia that keeps without refrigeration.
longDesc: Smoked fish is one of Tanzania's most important food preservation traditions — the abundance of Lake Victoria tilapia is preserved through smoking, allowing fish to be sold inland and kept without refrigeration.
ingredients: Wood chips or charcoal for smoking
steps: Score fish. Rub with salt and turmeric. Rest 30 minutes.
Set up a low charcoal or wood fire in a covered container with a rack above.
Fish is ready when golden, dry, and firm throughout.
Cool completely. Store in a dry place.
chefTips: Patience — low temperature over long time.
Fish should be dry and golden, not wet.
Use hardwood chips for cleaner smoke.
commonMistakes: Too high heat — cooks rather than smokes.
cookingScience: Smoking works through desiccation and chemical preservation — phenolic compounds in wood smoke inhibit microbial growth. Reduced water activity plus antimicrobial compounds allow weeks-long shelf life without refrigeration.
sustainabilityTips: Smoking preserves the Lake Victoria tilapia surplus, reducing waste.
storage: Up to 2 weeks at room temperature in a dry environment.
reheating: Flake into stews or warm in a pan.
culturalNote: Smoked fish is the food that connects coastal and inland Tanzania — preserved tilapia from Lake Victoria that travels to markets across the country.
